segments.t: As the draft officers escort a stunned Aleksandr away to serve in the army, Lyova happily takes back his sous-chef title and reinstates Max as a line cook. Meanwhile at the hospital, supplier Timur barges loudly into the ward and ruins Viktor Petrovich's latest attempt at playing weak for Elena.
Саша, иди на свое рабочее место.
Виктор Петрович не пришел в себя.
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'The question is, how did they track him down?' Barinov checks boldly with Max now, building the phrase around "vopros" ("question, matter") and "kak" ("how") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'Devil only knows.' Max displays an unhurried approach as the scene unfolds, combining "chert" ("darn, heck") and "znayet" ("knows") so the key meaning lands right away.
'By his last name, probably.' Sasha chooses a lively footing beside Barinov, pairing "familii" ("surname, last name") with "navernoye" ("probably") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'No, you will not do that, right?' Barinov presses quietly to make the point, combining "budesh" ("will") and "net" ("no") so the key meaning lands right away.
'You will not, all right then.' Max keeps a lively style as they talk, building the phrase around "budesh" ("will") and "ne" ("not") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'You are a line cook again.' Sasha sustains a steady style as the scene unfolds, joining "snova" ("again") to "povar" ("chef, cook") so every word pulls its weight.

'Sasha, go back to your workstation.' Barinov adopts a pointed mood as the scene unfolds, putting "idi" ("go") alongside "rabocheye" ("work") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Do you think I am constantly lying?' Max probes decisively in the scene, leaning on "dumayete" ("think") before closing the thought with "postoyanno" ("constantly").
'Oh, not at all!' Sasha holds a resolute view in the scene, weaving "da" ("yes") together with "nu" ("oh, come on") just the way native speakers do.
'Hello, my angel, Viktor...' Barinov sets a sharp angle as they talk, joining "zdravstvuyte" ("hello") to "angela" ("angel") so every word pulls its weight.
'Quiet, quiet, Timur.' Max picks a sharp tempo beside Barinov, weaving "tikho" ("easy, quiet") together with "timur" ("Timur") just the way native speakers do.

'Viktor Petrovich has not regained consciousness yet.' Sasha projects a natural direction as the scene unfolds, joining "prishel" ("came, arrived") to "viktor" ("Viktor") so every word pulls its weight.
'Could you please not shout in here?' Barinov wonders naturally to keep things clear, combining "mozhno" ("may, can") and "krichat" ("to shout") so the key meaning lands right away.

That wraps up this scene as with Aleksandr hauled off to the army, Lyova reinstates Max as a regular cook while Timur bursts into the hospital ward and ruins Barinov's second attempt at playing unconscious. Until next time!
